CHAPTER 08 / WEBFRONT

Embedding and distribution

Producing a resource header and building a standalone application.

Notation conventions

Function names, types, commands, options and filenames appear in monospace, for example describe, wf test or main.cpp. Italics introduce a term at its definition. Code blocks give the fragments to enter; the preceding text states their location and prerequisites.

Generating the resource header ↓Using the generated resources ↓Building the distribution version ↓

Generating the resource header

wf embed compiles the interface and packages its resources in a compressed C++ header. Notices for web dependencies are included. Run the following command in the application terminal.

Generating this header does not recompile the C++ programme. We shall perform that second step with CMake.

WEBFRONT TERMINAL
wf embed ui/main.tsx --output generated/LifeUI.hpp

Using the generated resources

The distribution programme no longer needs the project directory or the call to bootstrap. It uses the generated resource provider instead.

This fragment uses the Life example’s headers and assumes generated/LifeUI.hpp is on the include path. The repository supplies the corresponding WebFrontLifeEmbedded target.

C++23
#include "Life.hpp"
#include "LifeFrontend.hpp"
#include <webfront/WebFront.hpp>
#include "generated/LifeUI.hpp"

int main() {
    webfront::demo::LifeAppWithAssets<webfront::fs::LifeUI> app;
    app.cppFunction("life.step", &webfront::demo::nextLife);
    app.show();
}

Building the distribution version

Close the development window and run these commands in the same build directory. With Visual Studio, the executable is examples\Debug\WebFrontLifeEmbedded.exe.

The application can then run offline without interface sources or the tools cache. The rendering engine remains a platform dependency whose deployment must be arranged separately. wf embed does not produce an installer.

SYSTEM TERMINAL
cmake .. -DWEBFRONT_LIFE_ASSETS="$PWD/life-project/generated/LifeUI.hpp"
cmake --build . --target WebFrontLifeEmbedded
examples/WebFrontLifeEmbedded

↗ Exercise

Run the embedded version from an empty directory without network access. Check that your interface appears. Then read the chosen native engine’s requirements before preparing an installer.
